t: What DNA Digital Data Storage Is
title: What DNA Digital Data Storage Is
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: DNA digital data storage encodes binary data into synthesized DNA strands: files become sequences of A, C, G, T, stored as molecules in a tube. A gram of DNA can theoretically hold hundreds of petabytes, and DNA remains readable for thousands of years under proper conditions. This record is the entry point of the teaching ladder for DNA Digital Data Storage: start here, then move through the research state, the specifications, the public developments, the open challenges, and finally each piece needed to build it.
key_points: DNA Digital Data Storage in one line: DNA digital data storage encodes binary data into synthesized DNA strands: files become sequences of A, C, G, T, stored as molecules in a tube.
Why it matters: It is the densest storage medium known — the entire internet could fit in a shoebox..
Where it is used: cold archives, cultural preservation, deep backup, high-density data vaults..
Ladder rank 1 — the foundation. Everything else builds on this.

t: Current Research State of DNA Digital Data Storage
title: Current Research State of DNA Digital Data Storage
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Teams have stored books, images, operating systems, and video in DNA and read them back with sequencing. Research focuses on write speed (synthesis is slow and costly), random access via PCR primers, and error-correcting codes for synthesis/sequencing errors. Costs have fallen but remain far above tape; enzymatic synthesis promises faster, cheaper writing. Research moves in three waves: laboratory proof of concept, scaled prototypes under controlled conditions, and field trials. DNA Digital Data Storage currently sits at the stage described above, and the pieces records show what each wave still needs.
key_points: State of play: Teams have stored books, images, operating systems, and video in DNA and read them back with sequencing.
Leading approaches: phosphoramidite synthesis, enzymatic synthesis, PCR random access, fountain-code error correction.
Key institutions and programs: DNA storage startups, sequencing companies, university molecular-info labs.
What would change the timeline: the challenges record lists the blockers.
